key_insight: Learning to sample from an unknown Gibbs-optimal distribution is statistically different from choosing a single best action, and this shift turns regret from O(\sqrt{T}) into logarithmic growth under standard conditions.
engineering_relevance: For entropy-regularized RL, RLHF, and reward-guided generation, this gives a principled way to design samplers that stay close to the desired soft-optimal policy rather than merely optimizing one action.
method: Defines sampling regret as temperature-normalized cumulative KL to the target Gibbs distribution.
Develops two sampling analogues of bandit algorithms: UCS and TS^2.
Provides unified regret decompositions, including a Bayesian decomposition for posterior-random Gibbs targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret guarantees, including logarithmic-in-T bounds at fixed temperature and the first Bayesian sampling-regret decomposition.
watch_item: The logarithmic guarantees rely on fixed-temperature and standard uncertainty assumptions, so performance may degrade or require new analysis in low-temperature or highly misspecified settings.
paper_title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
